content.intro: Learn time zones and date storage through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Time Zones and Date Storage matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines time zones and date storage as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Time zone-aware datetimes; USE_TZ; Date and time field behavior; Local-time presentation; Handling daylight-saving transitions. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Time zone-aware datetimes
items.text: Store unambiguous instants using timezone-aware handling when appropriate, configure `USE_TZ`, and format for the user’s locale/time zone at presentation. Test daylight-saving boundaries.

items.text: For USE_TZ, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.text: Date and time field behavior affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.
